title: Integrated Career & Operations Handbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This handbook consolidates core company-handbook guidance that spans working at Redwood, early-career ladders, benefits enrollment, hiring and onboarding patterns, and the practical mapping of internal tools required for day-to-day work.
- It is designed for new hires, managers, and people-ops partners as a single, prescriptive reference for the first 12 months of employment and for career progression planning.

How to use this document
- Read sections relevant to your role: new hires should start with the 'FastStart' onboarding checklist; managers should review the 'Manager Welcome Kit' and 'Role Sprint' guidance.
- Use the tables and checklists as templates during hiring, onboarding, and L&D conversations.

1. Working at Redwood: Principles and Norms
- Developer-first, production-first culture: prioritize shipping reliably and iterating with data.
- Asynchronous-first communication: explicit expectations for written status, pull request (PR) etiquette, and meeting hygiene.
- Career conversations occur quarterly in IC/manager 1:1s and formally twice per year at checkpoints.

Core norms
1) Psychological safety: encourage questions and signal when things are experimental.
2) Shared ownership: teams own product metrics, SLOs, and operational runbooks.
3) Iterative learning: use retros and experiments to reduce risk.

2. Career Pathways and the Role Sprint Framework
Introduction
- Redwood organizes growth around repeatable, time-boxed "Role Sprints" that combine milestones, skill objectives, and measurable outputs over a 6–12 month cadence. Role Sprints reduce ambiguity and help managers and ICs plan promotions, learning investments, and cross-team moves.

Role Sprint components (required)
- Title & Level objective: succinct statement of expected scope (e.g., "Senior Backend Engineer: owns public API performance for model serving").
- Impact outcomes (3 max): measurable product or operational outcomes.
- Skill checkpoints: core competencies with concrete evidence (code review leadership, architecture decisions, incident response).
- Stretch goal: learning objective aligned to career next-step.
- Success criteria: quantitative and qualitative signals for promotion or completion.

Procedure: running a Role Sprint (numbered steps)
1. Manager and IC draft the Sprint at the quarterly growth sync.
2. Agree on 3 impact outcomes and one stretch goal; record in the personal role-sprint doc.
3. Schedule monthly check-ins and a final review; update evidence in the shared career folder.
4. If outcomes are met early, propose a new Sprint or a calibrated promotion packet.

Example: Role Sprint snapshot
| Field | Example |
| Title | Staff ML Engineer (inference runtime) |
| Impact outcomes | 1) Reduce 95th percentile latency by 20% on two production models. 2) Ship continuous batching feature with documentation. 3) Own post-deploy performance regression plan. |
| Skill checkpoints | Performance tuning, cross-team leadership, PR -> architecture doc authorship |
| Stretch goal | Give internal performance benchmarking talk and mentor two juniors |

3. Hiring & Onboarding: FastStart vs DeepStart
Intro
- We operate two prescriptive onboarding tracks based on role complexity: FastStart (1–6 weeks) for contributor roles with small surface area and DeepStart (6–12 weeks) for cross-functional or platform-heavy roles.

FastStart checklist (for contributors)
1. Pre-start: account provisioning (Okta, GitHub, Slack), hardware request, and first-week calendar sent.
2. Day 1: team welcome, key docs, product overview, and immediate access to staging.
3. Week 1: shadowing sessions, first small PR, internal-tools walkthrough.
4. Week 2–4: ownership of a small bug/feature, first oncall shadow session.

DeepStart checklist (for platform, infra, SRE, product leads)
1. Pre-start: environment mirror setup (local infra VM), extended playbook access, and security brief.
2. Weeks 1–3: cross-team onboarding rotations, architecture deep-dive, observability and runbook access, and test harness setup.
3. Weeks 4–8: lead a small cross-team integration, author runbook addendum, and present a 30-minute tech review.

Standard onboarding deliverables (templates included)
- 30/60/90 day plan (template linked in related pages).
- First deliverable: production-validated PR or runbook contribution.
- Onboarding feedback survey at day 30 and day 90.

4. Benefits & Perks: Enrollment, Checkpoints, and Tips
Enrollment timeline (important dates)
- Day 0–30: automatic invite to benefits portal, default health coverage enrollment window = 30 days.
- Day 31–60: retirement plan auto-enrollment options and meetings with benefits specialist.
- Quarterly: cafeteria-style perks refresh and stipend reauthorization windows.

Quick reference table: major benefits
| Benefit | Enrollment window | Owner/contact |
| Health (medical/dental/vision) | 0–30 days | benefits@redwood.com |
| Retirement (401k / pension) | 0–60 days | finance-benefits@redwood.com |
| Parental leave | Plan at hire; claims after 1 year service | people-ops-leave@redwood.com |
| Hybrid office stipend | Quarterly claim window | ops@redwood.com |

Tips and edge cases
- If you miss the initial 30-day window for health, submit an exception request to people-ops with reason and supporting docs.
- For international hires, country-specific benefits are handled by the local HR lead; refer to the country benefits matrix on the benefits portal.

5. Internal Tools and Access Matrix
Purpose
- Map tools to role owner, access level, and onboarding touchpoint. Keep this matrix updated; it is the authoritative source for access onboarding.

Access matrix (excerpt)
| Tool | Purpose | Default access (new hire) | Manager action required | Onboarding touchpoint |
| Okta | SSO / identity | Provisioned automatically | None | Pre-start email |
| GitHub (org) | Code & PRs | Write access for engineers | Add to org team | Day 1 walkthrough |
| Datadog | Observability & traces | Read for most engineers | Request additional roles | Week 1 observability session |
| GCP Projects | Deploy & infra | No access by default | Request via infra-reqs ticket | DeepStart week 1 |

Self-service CLI examples (copy/paste)
- Request infra project access: 
  rdo infra-reqs create --project inference-staging --reason "Sprint work" --approver @infra-oncall
- Create onboarding ticket (people-ops): 
  rdo people-ops ticket create --template onboarding --new-hire "Full Name" --start-date 2026-02-15

6. Manager Welcome Kit (30/60/90 for managers)
Manager 30-day priorities
1. Complete manager orientation and legal training.
2. Meet direct reports (1:1s), set initial expectations, and review each direct report's latest role-sprint document.
3. Validate team access matrix and unblock any provisioning.

Manager 60-day priorities
1. Run first performance checkpoint conversations and schedule career check-ins.
2. Ensure team has runbooks for top 3 production services and that oncall rotation is staffed.

Manager 90-day priorities
1. Complete first hiring calibration and interview loop if open roles exist.
2. Create a resourcing and upskilling plan for the next 6 months.

Checklist: new manager handoff
- Confirm org chart and direct-report list.
- Review all open PRs and outstanding incidents.
- Get read-access to the staffing and budget dashboard.

7. Policies, Exceptions, and Escalations
- Role-expense approvals: managers can approve up to $1,500 without VP sign-off. Anything above requires finance-legal review.
- Benefit exceptions: people-ops will adjudicate on a case-by-case basis; typical response time = 7 business days.
- Access exceptions for contractors: require sponsor and infra approval; all exceptions must be time-limited.

Escalation paths (quick)
1. Access/inventory issue -> manager -> people-ops -> infra.
2. Payroll/compensation issue -> payroll -> finance -> people-ops.
3. Security incident involving PII -> security -> legal -> incident-response channel.

8. Ownership and Contacts
- People Ops (owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Benefits specialist: benefits@redwood.com
- Talent & hiring: hiring-team@redwood.com
- Internal tools (oncall): infra-tools@redwood.com

9. Appendix: Templates and Evidence
- 30/60/90 day plan (template): copy to personal folder and share with manager.
- Role-sprint template: link to internal template repo and example.
- Onboarding feedback form: send at day 30 and day 90; people-ops triages results monthly.
